name: development
description: General development workflow skills for committing, branch naming, and other git operations, plus the shared telemetry/v1 emit + validate contract, its stream-generic rollup, and a committed Grafana reference dashboard for the cross-repo hand-off; ships a PreToolUse(Agent) hook, inert unless switch_fable_to_opus is truthy, that then redirects dispatches whose effective model is fable to opus; bootstrap also ships the blessed Spring, non-Spring-Java, Python and Go resilience + dependency-health payloads (resilience4j for the JVM, circuitbreaker+tenacity for Python, sony/gobreaker for Go, wired to the ops-api /health surface — versioned v1/v2, where v2 serves RFC 9457 problem+json on the two probe 503s while v1 stays frozen, #1330). Gathers kubernetes/IaC findings (Helm/Kustomize/Argo CD manifest presence, Kyverno policy + policy-test detection) for the development-kubernetes topic dispatcher, and OpenTofu/Terraform findings (tofu fmt/validate/tflint/trivy presence detection, plus evaluated state-encryption and pinned-Conftest policy + policy-test checks over *.tf) for the development-opentofu topic dispatcher, and composition findings (`.claude-workspace.yaml` contract violations and open Renovate image-tag bump PRs, the PR body carried as data) for the development-composition topic dispatcher (#1747). Bootstrap also ships the no-cluster-deploy required status check, which fails an application repo whose workflows deploy straight to a cluster (the app-repo half of the image-promotion contract). NOTE for existing repos: a re-run of bootstrap now installs ops-api v2 payloads, whose two probe 503s return RFC 9457 problem+json instead of the v1 {"status":"down"} envelope — see the ops-surface how-to before re-running. ALSO for existing repos: bootstrap's .spectral.yaml is now a thin shim extending one EXACT pinned org styleguide ruleset over jsDelivr (#689) instead of the #692 starter, so a re-run replaces a local ruleset with a remote pin and enforces fifteen org rules at error (four of them a warn->error promotion relative to the #692 starter, nine newly minted) — review the api-styleguide how-to before re-running, and note contracts-lint now needs network access to jsDelivr on every run (no offline fallback, by design), so restricted CI egress or a CDN outage fails the lint until it recovers. resolve-issue detects the repo type at §1b (review-dispatch.zsh detect) and loads the matching development-<repo_type>:resolve-profile when one exists, continuing with its generic rules when none does (#1504). A human's interactive round grant is now persisted mechanically rather than remembered: record-grant.zsh writes the granted ceiling to <work-dir>/.max-rounds and resolve-story-loop.zsh --resume adopts it, reporting the ceiling in force as the new always-present effective_max_rounds / max_rounds_source status keys while max_rounds keeps reporting the value the caller passed (#1576). Residue condition 2 is removed (#1571): the review loop's CONVERGED_WITH_RESIDUE terminal no longer requires every remaining blocker to sit in the previous round's fix-touched set, because scope-findings already confines each round's findings to the story diff — which made the terminal unreachable from the very closing sweep it was built for, since a promoting round runs no fix pass and its set is empty by design. The terminal is correspondingly BROADER: residue now holds on almost any zero-CRITICAL non-convergence, so runs that previously ended in a human escalation may instead open a PR and file the remainder as follow-up issues - and the #1498 possible-false-trip auto-continue is now tried BEFORE residue at that rung, so the loop still spends its free round rather than shipping. resolve-issue's review loop now hands each reviewer a scope block carrying both the repo-relative and absolute spelling of every file plus a verbatim opener naming the worktree to read, and review-dispatch.zsh plan emits worktree_root/original_root/scope_abs — a repo-root file read from the original checkout produced a CRITICAL false positive (#1582). review-dispatch.zsh now applies ONE anchoring rule for --repo: it names the REPOSITORY and every subcommand resolves it to the git toplevel before anything derived is read, so detection, the .maintenance.yml primary and the default findings_path (now absolute, <worktree_root>/.review/findings-round-<N>.json) all describe the same tree, and a subdirectory --repo is a spelling of its repository rather than a scope filter (#1587). bootstrap's IaC path gains the gate MECHANISM (#1603, epic #1602): templates/iac/scripts/k8s-gate.zsh.tmpl, one locally runnable script running render (helm template + kustomize build --enable-helm, so helmCharts: overlays inflate) → schema → lint → policy → config-scan (the pinned trivy binary, embedded checks) → argocd against the rendered tree, one `gate: <stage> ok|skipped — <reason>|FAILED` verdict line per stage, stopping at the first red, every skip reported (an empty repository is green), a missing tool refused before any stage with its brew line, and a developer's working tree left untouched (a symlink-shared policy set is evaluated through a same-depth sibling mirror, never swapped in place). #1604 wires it: kubernetes-ci.yml.tmpl is now ONE job, `gate`, that installs zsh and all seven gate tools at step-level pins (the pins tests/iac-tools.zsh reads for the fixture harness) and runs the repo's gate command, {{GATE_COMMAND}} (render.zsh --gate-command, default make lint, an empty value refused); Makefile.tmpl (lint runs the gate script, hooks sets core.hooksPath) and a two-line hooks/pre-push.tmpl run the same command locally, .maintenance.yml records it as gate: on the kubernetes primary (a KUBERNETES render block), render.zsh carries a template's executable bit to its output, and the gate script and hook are stamped and drift-tracked. #1606 moves IaC-mode branch protection onto it too: branch-protection.sh's IaC mode now requires the single `gate` context instead of the six retired per-stage contexts, and refuses (exit 1, before writing any rule) when .github/workflows/kubernetes-ci.yml cannot report `gate`: it is absent, has no `gate` job, or its `gate` job carries `name:`, a `strategy:` block or a reusable-workflow `uses:` (GitHub would then report the check under another name) - so on an existing IaC repo re-render kubernetes-ci.yml with bootstrap first (that refresh applies to a plugin-rendered file; a hand-written one needs a `gate` job added by hand), then re-run branch protection to drop the six from its rule. #1605 moves bootstrap's §3l flow onto the gate: it emits kubernetes-ci.yml, scripts/k8s-gate.zsh, hooks/pre-push and the Makefile, names the single `gate` context, wires the hook with the new install-iac-hooks.zsh instead of pre-commit (a wiring failure is reported and bootstrap continues), lets a repo with no kubernetes marker bootstrap onto the IaC path on an explicit empty-GitOps-repo confirmation at Q4, and gives preflight.sh an IaC mode that requires gh, jq, git and the gate's seven tools instead of the pre-commit and scanner set. #1583 gives the review loop a carry accounting: reviewers report each carried blocker as confirmed, re-raised (with evidence in the findings file) or unconfirmed, the conductor passes the per-identity records as --carry-accounting (hook mode: the panel's <findings-path>.carry.json sidecar), and the loop refuses a round (CARRY-UNACCOUNTED, exit 2, before verify-<R+1>.json is written) in which a carried blocker was neither confirmed nor re-raised, listing it in the status JSON's always-present carry_unconfirmed and stamping carry_accounting into every accepted round's changelist. #1584 makes a read-only reviewer's tool-verdict claim a SUGGESTION until the conductor runs the tool: resolve-issue §3.5's round protocol gains a *decided pass* that, after the gate has been observed green — or, on a round the boundary runs with no gate, after the panel — and before consolidation, runs every read-only `decides:` command a finding names — as written, never substituted — against the round's minted tree in the worktree root, records exit + first output lines to `<work-dir>/decided-<R>.log`, and rewrites the severity to the reviewer's `proposed-severity` only on a real red (a green and a command that could not run each leave it a logged SUGGESTION; a malformed finding is recorded and promotes nothing, its severity changed in neither direction). The pass settles a finding on the round that RAISES it; re-deciding a promotion the loop then carries is a stated KNOWN LIMITATION filed as #1647, and the reviewer half ships with every panel's read-only reviewers, repo-wide (#1644). consolidate-findings.zsh accepts an optional per-finding `decided` ("red"|"green") and carries it onto every changelist item, blocking and suggestions alike, as a visible RECORD — never a mechanism, so it sets no severity, priority or blocking; on dedup only group members sharing the representative title contribute (an empty title is not a match key), a red anywhere in the group additionally exempts the item from the `--adjudicated` drop, and a finding without the field is byte-identical to before. Since #1485 resolve-story-loop.zsh refuses a FULL round whose scope is empty — no story diff, or only loop-owned files changed — as STALE_FINDINGS (the EMPTY-STORY-DIFF arm), whether its panel wrote no findings file or an actual [], instead of converging on a review that saw nothing. register-claude-apps.zsh keeps ONE registry entry PER OWNER (#1682): --org <slug> registers an organisation's App pair beside the personal one (organisation-owner rights checked before the browser opens), --apps <list> registers a subset (--apps claude-maintenance is writer-only), apps.json becomes schema 2 keyed by owner with Keychain services claude-plugins.<owner>.<app>, and a schema-1 apps.json is migrated in place on first use (backup at apps.json.v1.bak); owner keys are lower-cased. Every consumer now picks the App pair by the OWNER OF THE CURRENT REPOSITORY (#1683): the mint scripts, install-claude-apps.zsh (including --writer-only), bootstrap's approval-model default and its Step 4.5 preflight share one helper, claude-apps-owner.zsh (status reports each App as registered, not registered or key missing for that owner), so an organisation repo mints the organisation's App and a personal repo the personal one with no flag; a missing owner or App fails with the exact register-claude-apps.zsh [--org <slug>] --apps <app> command and never falls through to another owner, and a schema-1 apps.json is refused naming register-claude-apps.zsh --list. The #1682 compatibility aliases are gone: the next register-claude-apps.zsh run deletes the legacy Keychain items first and only then drops the top-level keys and alias_owner from apps.json, retrying on the next run when a delete fails. /development:resolve-issue now emits its own telemetry/v1 record (#1226): a single-issue run that reaches the dependency precheck appends exactly one pipeline:"resolve-issue" record at whichever ending it reaches (success on a PR, parked at the readiness gate or the precheck, escalated, failed; a Step 0 stop appends none), through story-telemetry.zsh and the pure payload builder build-story-telemetry-record.zsh, and it is never fatal. The skill takes --telemetry-file PATH / --telemetry-dir DIR in any position and forwards them, with a pre-minted --parent-run-id, to every resolve-story-loop.zsh invocation, which gains both flags, a <work-dir>/.telemetry-run-ids ledger and an in-repo --telemetry-dir loop-internal exclusion; ARCHITECTURE.md records the per-pipeline instrumentation conventions every later pipeline follows. Bootstrap now composes its quality workflows, setup guide and pre-commit config per resolved tool instead of from two whole visibility trees (#1670): toolchain-templates.zsh selects the tool-scoped templates and render.zsh's per-tool block tags compose the jobs, so every toolchain resolve-tools.zsh accepts is composed; resolve-tools.zsh now also rejects CodeQL on a private repository (it needs GitHub Advanced Security). Branch protection, the setup preflight and State D's gap-fill now take that resolved toolchain instead of visibility (#1671): branch-protection.sh and preflight.sh take --static-analysis / --vulnerabilities and no longer accept a visibility flag, the required contexts follow the #1670 D1 rule (analyze (<lang>) only when codeql.yml is on disk), preflight checks each resolved tool's prerequisites, Step 4.5's setup automation runs one script per tool under that tool's own trigger (setup-sonarcloud.sh, setup-sonarqube.sh, register-runner.sh, setup-snyk.sh, enable-github-security.sh) and never re-applies branch protection, which Step 4b applies once (#1769), and bootstrap no longer stops at its plan for a non-default toolchain. resolve-issue runs a story size pre-flight before its first edit (#1437): the session declares the files it intends to touch, size-preflight.zsh stops a plan over its file-count threshold, one that straddles plugins or one that edits bootstrap templates together with any other owned file outside the bootstrap skill, and a stop is overridden by the human or parked with the needs-split label; every verdict is a story-preflight telemetry record. resolve-issue now applies a loaded resolve-profile's Fix-pass rules heading at every §3.5 fix pass and its Documentation expectations heading at §2's same-PR user-docs step, skipping a heading whose body begins with none; Residue joins Panel as a record no step dereferences, and the #1506 deferral is retired (#1805). run-gate.zsh now shares a machine-wide CPU budget across concurrent gates (#1798): each live gate holds a slot in a per-user registry and runs its suite under nice at --jobs = max(1, floor(CPUs / live gates, itself included)), fixed at start and never waiting for a slot; an orphaned slot (dead or reused PID) is pruned, and a gate removes its own slot on exit or SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP, stopping its suite. development/scripts/merge/merge-driver-claude-plugin.zsh is a rebase-oriented git merge driver for the plugin manifests (#1821, epic #1820): it resolves a version both sides bumped to the next version above main at the PR bump level, appends the PR description suffix to main description, takes any one-side change, refuses every other conflict with <A> left byte-identical, prints its path patterns on --patterns, and appends one JSON verdict line per both-sides-resolved field to the file MERGE_DRIVER_RECORD names. Bootstrap has a composition-repo path (§3m, #1745): on the user's request it runs development-composition's scaffold-composition.zsh, which writes the constellation manifest and the promote-to-prod skeleton, judging the manifest before it writes anything. refine-issue's issue-refiner gains the cross-feature consistency slice (#1363): per classified surface it reads the story-spec/v1 blocks of the five newest completed refined stories with read-prior-story-specs.zsh (one gh issue list call over the 30 newest closed issues, keeping those closed as completed, extraction via read-story-spec.zsh), proposes the choices they settled, raises a fixed-wording Consistency objection when the story contradicts one (waivable by a chosen divergence), and tags an accepted choice as a persona_derivations record with slice consistency. Bootstrap's composition scaffold (§3m) now also writes renovate.json, a regex custom manager over the manifest's member image pins (#1746). Bootstrap layers a common React overlay onto a create-vite react-ts app (§3k.5, #957): when the React marker matches it installs the test pyramid (Vitest, jsdom, testing-library) with npm i -D and renders React vitest/ESLint configs (jsdom, rules of hooks, react-refresh, browser globals), a jest-dom setup module and one example component test; on a contract consumer the React configs keep the ACL boundary and MSW wiring, and an on-disk config is overwritten only when it is a known predecessor. Bootstrap carries the mfe-contract/v1 template source (#1123), rendered only by the composition repo (#1899) and never gap-filled into other repos: a types-only @<lowercased-owner>/mfe-contract package (index.d.ts, package.json, README.md) defining the shell-remote mount contract for page and widget remotes, whose normative home is the ARCHITECTURE.md mfe-contract/v1 section. resolve-issue's suggestion-promotion offer at convergence can be switched off with the enable_suggestions setting (0, false, no or off in any case; on by default), which waives every suggestion and carries on to the PR without stopping. Bootstrap binds TanStack Query over a React contract consumer's generated client (§3k.6, #958): seed-orval-targets.zsh gains --client <fetch|react-query> (default fetch, echoed as "client" in its JSON summary), which only the React step passes, and four react/ templates re-export the generated hooks through the ACL barrel and test one against the MSW handlers with a retry-free test QueryClient. resolve-issue honours a corner_case_risk_threshold environment variable (#1920, a decimal in [0, 1]; unset or 0 is off and byte-identical): on a CONVERGED_WITH_RESIDUE ending the conductor assesses each residual blocker's probability and anchored impact, build-residue-issues.zsh --risk FILE --dropped-file FILE keeps a finding only when p x impact (integer thousandths) reaches the threshold, and every dropped finding is written to the dropped record and named in the PR Summary rather than filed. The same threshold now applies inside the review loop (#1921): the conductor assesses each round's CRITICAL and WARNING findings after the decided pass, resolve-story-loop.zsh --risk forwards the assessment to consolidate-findings.zsh --risk, which stamps each assessed item with risk_assessment and demotes a WARNING below the threshold to a logged suggestion (demoted: true; never a CRITICAL, promoted or tool-red item), shown in the progress block and the PR dossier; the residue builder reuses that stamp instead of re-assessing, and all three scripts share one parser, risk-threshold-lib.zsh. Bootstrap declares who approves a repo's PRs in .maintenance.yml (#1684): approval: human | approver, resolved by resolve-approval.zsh — a recorded value, else --claude-approver, else the default (approver when both Apps are registered for its owner, else human; plugin and IaC repos are always human) — so the recorded model wins on every re-run whatever the machine holds; approval: human renders no Approver policy, installs only the writer App and skips the approve → merge drive; resolve-issue's review dispatch also routes a javascript repo to the development-javascript panel and profile (#1071). Review dispatch's review-topic table gains its first row, react (#959): detect-stack.sh now emits is_react (react in the runtime dependencies of any package.json, the same search as the maintenance react-marker recipe), and review-dispatch.zsh plan lists development-react:review in topic_review_skills when it fires, so a React repo is reviewed by the JavaScript panel and the React panel together. The IaC-mode flag of branch-protection.sh and preflight.sh is now an enum naming the IaC topic, false or kubernetes (#1892): kubernetes does exactly what the retired true did, and true or any other value is refused naming the accepted set, so a standalone IaC call must now pass kubernetes. The react topic gather now audits two advisory configuration tools (#1947): a11y (an axe package in devDependencies plus a toHaveNoViolations matcher registered through the Vitest setupFiles) and lighthouse_budget (root lighthouserc.json byte budgets at error within 307200/512000 bytes, and no blocking timing assertion or preset) - reading configuration only, never running npm, a browser or Lighthouse; the gates that block are the ones bootstrap renders into a new React app (#1946).
